articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 Turbo with Native Multimodal Reasoning Across Code, Vision, and Audio
articles.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 Turbo, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning that can jointly process code repositories, visual diagrams, and spoken instructions in a single inference pass. Benchmarks show a 38% improvement on SWE-Bench over GPT-5 base and near-human performance on graduate-level scientific reasoning tasks. The model also introduces a new structured chain-of-thought API for enterprise customers needing auditable reasoning traces.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Frontier Math and Protein Interaction Prediction
articles.summary: DeepMind announced Gemini Ultra 2 with breakthrough results on the FrontierMath benchmark, solving 85% of problems that previously stumped all AI systems. The model also integrates an updated AlphaFold module capable of predicting multi-protein complex interactions with experimentally validated accuracy, opening new avenues for drug discovery pipelines.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Limited Deployment in BMW and Amazon Warehouses
articles.summary: Tesla's third-generation Optimus humanoid robot has entered limited commercial deployment at BMW manufacturing plants and Amazon fulfillment centers, handling bin-picking, parts transport, and light assembly tasks. The Gen 3 units feature improved dexterous manipulation with 22-DOF hands and an on-device vision-language model enabling natural language task instruction from floor supervisors.

articles.title: Figure AI Raises $1.5B Series C, Demonstrates Autonomous Multi-Robot Coordination in Factory Trials
articles.summary: Figure AI closed a $1.5 billion Series C round at an $18 billion valuation after demonstrating its Figure 03 humanoid robots autonomously coordinating complex multi-step assembly workflows without human orchestration. The system uses a shared world model and decentralized planning architecture that allows up to 12 robots to dynamically allocate tasks and recover from failures in real time.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Constitutional AI Monitoring Framework for Critical Infrastructure Deployments
articles.summary: Anthropic released an open-source Constitutional AI Monitoring (CAIM) framework designed for deploying LLM-based agents in critical infrastructure contexts such as power grids and healthcare systems. The framework provides formal verification of agent behavior boundaries, real-time constraint satisfaction monitoring, and automated rollback mechanisms, addressing a key barrier to enterprise AI adoption in regulated industries.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm GAA Process Node, First Chips Slated for AI Accelerators
articles.summary: TSMC announced volume production of its N1.4 process node using next-generation gate-all-around transistor architecture at its Kaohsiung fab. First customers include NVIDIA and Broadcom for next-generation AI accelerator chips expected in Q2 2027, promising a 25% power efficiency improvement and 15% performance uplift over the current N2 node.

articles.title: Microsoft and Quantinuum Demonstrate Fault-Tolerant Logical Qubit Operations Below Error Correction Threshold
articles.summary: Microsoft and Quantinuum jointly published results showing sustained fault-tolerant operations on 32 logical qubits with error rates below the threshold needed for practical quantum error correction. This milestone, achieved on Quantinuum's H3 trapped-ion system paired with Microsoft's Majorana-based topological qubits, represents a significant step toward commercially useful quantum computation for materials science and cryptography applications.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics Atlas Now Performs Full Automotive Subassembly with Tool Use and Bimanual Coordination
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics showcased its electric Atlas robot performing end-to-end automotive subassembly tasks including torque-wrench fastening, sealant application, and connector insertion using bimanual coordination with force-feedback tooling. The system leverages a new sim-to-real transfer pipeline trained on over 50 billion simulation steps, dramatically reducing the time needed to teach new assembly sequences from weeks to hours.
